comment: ai-antispam's own lanes and the events each may write (#193). registry/factories/ai-antispam.json declares this factory's lane roles; `hq` and `triage` are in the core matrix, and the three below are the factory's own. They are the same KIND of lane -- take a unit, settle it, report -- so the set is uniform on purpose; a differentiated one would encode a distinction no measurement supports. MEMBERSHIP AND AUTHORIZATION ARE BOTH REQUIRED: `actors` grants membership and `by_event` grants authorization, and a lane declared here for membership but absent from `by_event` resolves and is then refused BY NAME. Measured 2026-09-28: before this file existed, two of this factory's five lanes resolved through the fragment and were then refused at append (`bot`, `outreach`), so migrating tools/ledger.py to the template basis left them unable to write a ledger row at all. NOT GRANTED, each for a stated reason: `intake` and `dispatch` are Triage's rows (SKILL.md section 4), so a lane that files a board item still owes Triage its intake leg -- the four unauthorized intake rows the schema gate reds on are that defect (agent-factories#156), never a licence; `ruling` is the process owner's, `score` is Surveys' measurement duty, and `genesis` is bootstrap-only. DECLARED 2026-11-20: `release`. The event itself is lawful and by design -- docs/ledger-refs-kinds.json declares it (the kit declares it too) because the write path implements the withdrawal verb and `verify` prints "A withdrawal is recorded as a `release` naming this row" for every open claim. What was MISSING was the AUTHORIZATION: AUTHORIZED_ACTORS_BY_EVENT has no `release` key in the kit or here, so authorized_for_event returns (), and the write-path guard (tools/ledger.py:1207, `if authorized and actor_origin == "derived"`) SKIPS because an empty tuple is falsy. Any lane could release any claim, and a release WITHDRAWS another lanes claim -- so an ungated release can silence the open-claim answer that tells a reader in-flight from abandoned. The actor set is the AUTHORITY set, not the claiming set: measured over all 20 release rows in this ledger the actors are hq 15 and triage 5 and nobody else, so this refuses no row ever written while closing the hole for every lane that is not an authority. A lane that wants to abandon its OWN claim asks HQ or Triage to stamp the release -- the same convention already used for `intake` and `dispatch`, and deliberate here because the guard is event+actor only and cannot express "only your own claim". Reported to the kit owner: the same key is absent from the shared matrix while the shared tool implements the verb.
